The song file stops at the switch, **2:40.73**. Wherever this brief says ~1:57, rescale the chapter bounds to the real 160.73 s. > - The files: `public/audio/music-ending.mp3` (to the switch); `music-ending-loop.mp3` (three copies of the 8-bar instrumental chorus, loop the middle one with `levels.json` start..end); `music-ending-overclocked.mp3` (1.2x speed, pitch up). > - Start the loop source exactly when the song source ends, on the same `AudioContext` clock. `outro.json` is written by `scripts/music-outro.py` into `zips/runworld/music/outro-final/`; the game reads `levels.json`. > - **The pre-built files** are in `arena-gathered/argo-relay/` (see its `TRIAGE.md`): land, review and wire them; don't paste. Drive the picture from `AudioContext.currentTime`, not `performance.now()`. > **File Destination in Repo:** `docs/prompts/sidecar/33-credits-video.md` > **Source Plan:** `docs/argo/plans/30-credits-video.md` & `docs/argo/plans/26b-ending-song-v2.md` > **Target Branch:** `main` (Post-`TASK-24` Polish Wave) > **Audio Assets:** > - Main Ending Track: `1.2x` time-stretched (pitch-kept) **v4b** at **144 BPM** (`~117 s` vocal run) > - Instrumental Loop Metadata: `outro.json` generated by `scripts/music-outro.py` (`loopStart`, `loopEnd`, `bpm: 144`) > - Bonus Lab Monitor Replay Track: `1.2x` pitch-up version titled **`"Four Floats (Overclocked)"`** ## Context & Goal Build a real-time, deterministic in-engine credits music video in `apps/web/src/credits/` that plays automatically upon completing Act IX (`A9-03`) and can be replayed anytime from the Main Menu (`[Credits]`) or the Lab's `old-monitor`. # 30 — Real-Time In-Engine Credits Music Video Plan ("Four Floats" v2)

> **File Destination in Repo:** `docs/argo/plans/30-credits-video.md`
> **Author:** Gemini Argo (Creative Lead) & Claude Opus (Engineering Lead)
> **Origin:** Owner Directive (`OWNER_ASKS.md`, 14 October 2026: *"if you can make an animation that plays over the credits"*, referencing the code-driven chapter approach of [JohnHeibel/PDoomVideo](https://github.com/JohnHeibel/PDoomVideo/blob/main/README.md))
> **Audio Track:** `"Four Floats"` v2 (`docs/argo/plans/26b-ending-song-v2.md`, `140 s` main track at 120 BPM + Demucs-separated looping instrumental chorus outro)
> **Target Brief:** Fold into **Sidecar Brief 28** (`28-lab-choreography-and-vista.md`) or standalone **Sidecar Brief 33** (`33-credits-video.md`)
> **Date:** 14 October 2026
> **Status:** **APPROVED FOR IMPLEMENTATION.**

## 1. Architecture: Code-Driven Chapters Rendered Live In-Engine (60 FPS)

Inspired by the modular timeline structure of [JohnHeibel/PDoomVideo](https://github.com/JohnHeibel/PDoomVideo/blob/main/README.md) (`src/ch/` one chapter per song section driven by a shared `timeline.ts` clock) and the split-screen telemetry layout of [Valve's Portal Credits](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/wiki/Credits.txt), our credits sequence is **not** a pre-rendered MP4 video that would bloat the repository. Instead, it is a **real-time, deterministic in-engine music video (`apps/web/src/credits/`)** driven by `audioContext.currentTime` (with a `performance.now()` fallback when offline):

    apps/web/src/credits/
      index.ts                # Mounts the credits director, audio sync clock, and skip/replay controls
      timeline.ts             # Shared 120 BPM beat grid, chapter boundaries, and lyric cue timestamps from 26b
      credits-hud.tsx         # Stage-reactive lyric pill (left) + scrolling credits roll (right)
      ch/
        ch1-cold-boot.ts      # 0:00–0:22 | Stage 0a Wireframe: Lab wake, breaker throw, wireframe Moon
        ch2-one-bit-facets.ts # 0:22–0:44 | Stage 0b -> 1 EGA: Radial facet fill, Beam mining, 12 kW brownout
        ch3-chorus-bloom.ts   # 0:44–1:06 | Stage 2 VGA: "Four floats in the dark" 4-plume quartet & grass
        ch4-archive-rifts.ts  # 1:06–1:28 | Stage 3 Gouraud: 2D sprites -> 3D .md1 brutes, Vance ridge, Rover jump
        ch5-window-heal.ts    # 1:28–1:52 | Stage 4–5 Hydro/Coverage: Lake flood, Combiner splice, Breach zips shut
        ch6-suitcam-finale.ts # 1:52–2:20 | Stage 6 Suit-Cam PBR: First-person iris blowout, forest, 11 domes
        ch7-outro-loop.ts     # 2:20–Loop | Instrumental Chorus Loop: Healed Lab/Moon dual-world diptych hold

### Why Real-Time In-Engine Wins
1. **Zero Video Megabytes (`Rule 3` & `POL-27`):** Uses our already-loaded Lab, Gate, Plot, Avatar, Machine, and Monster scenes plus our `Brief 27` post-processing shader—adding `< 12 KB` of TypeScript camera/state keyframes to `dist/index.html`.
2. **Uses the Player's Own Plot & Custom Scientist:** Because it runs in-engine, Astro wears the player's actual chosen **Visor Color** and custom **Avatar Name**, and the final shots showcase the player's actual built outpost.
3. **Interactive Camera & Replayability:** The player can watch hands-free, nudge the camera gently with the mouse (`+-8°` parallax), scroll the credits roll with the mouse wheel, or replay the music video anytime from the Main Menu (`[Credits]`) or the Lab's `old-monitor` (`Plan 29` §2.10).

## 2. Screen Layout: Viewport, Stage-Skinned Lyric Pill & Credits Roll

To ensure the 3D choreography, the synced lyrics, and the credits roll never collide (`Plan 16` / `Brief 25`):

| Screen Region | Coordinates | Visual Behavior & `data-fidelity` Skinning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Full 3D Viewport** | `100% × 100%` (Camera framed on the left `62%` rule-of-thirds center) | Renders the active chapter's 3D scene through the exact stage shader (`Stage 0a` Wireframe $\to$ `Stage 6` Suit-Cam CMOS PBR) matching the song's current timestamp. |
| **Top-Left Telemetry Badge** | `top: 24px, left: 24px` | Displays the live stage readout (`[STAGE 0a // VECTOR WIREFRAME]` $\to$ `[STAGE 6 // SUIT-CAM CMOS PBR]`), Dr. Haddy's CRT radio portrait (pulsing gently on vocal syllables), and a 4-bar (`Pxd, Vtx, Lx, Aq`) chiptune spectrum analyzer. |
| **Bottom-Left Lyric Caption Card** | `bottom: 36px, left: 36px` (`max-width: 560px`) | **Uses the active `data-fidelity` skin from `Plan 28`!** Morphs with a `120 ms` glitch flash at each chapter boundary (`0a` hairline vector box $\to$ `0b` 1-bit dithered Mac card $\to$ `1` EGA double-line box $\to$ `2` VGA chiseled bevel $\to$ `3` Gouraud slate $\to$ `4-6` frosted Suit-Cam visor glass). Highlights each 5- and 7-syllable line on the 120 BPM beat. |
| **Right-Third Credits Roll** | `top: 0, right: 32px, width: 360px, height: 100%` | A sleek, semi-transparent vertical telemetry column (`--hud-bg`, `--hud-border`, `--hud-font-body` from the current `data-fidelity` skin) scrolling upward at `28 px/s` with top/bottom alpha feathering. |

## 3. Shot-by-Shot Storyboard Synced to `"Four Floats"` v2 (`0:00` to Loop)

> **Note for Opus:** Rough timestamps (`mm:ss`) below map to the `140 s` 120 BPM v2 track (`26b-ending-song-v2.md`) plus the Demucs-separated looping instrumental chorus outro. Snap each `tStart` / `tEnd` constant in `timeline.ts` to the exact bar/beat markers once the audio cut finishes.

- **HUD Skin:** `data-fidelity="0a"` (1 px phosphor-white wireframe boxes, hollow vector bars).

Camera tilts down as Astro's hand reaches for the glowing red console button—Dr. Haddy's CRT portrait pops in top-left with a warning flash—and Astro instead pulls the **Power Wall Breaker**. ### Chapter 2 — 1-Bit Facets, Dirt Mining & The 12 kW Brownout (`0:22 – 0:44`)
- **Visual Look:** **`Stage 0b` — 1-Bit Flat-Faceted Dither** (`0:22–0:33`) $\to$ **`Stage 1` — 16-Color EGA Mineral Facets** (`0:33–0:44`).
- **HUD Skin:** `data-fidelity="0b"` (1-bit Macintosh/Obra Dinn checkerboard header) $\to$ `data-fidelity="1"` (EGA double-border TUI).

# 26 — Act IX Finale & Credits Song Plan: "Four Floats (Not Really Dirt)"

> **File Destination in Repo:** `docs/argo/plans/26-ending-song.md`
> **Author:** Gemini Argo (Creative Lead) & Claude Opus (Engineering Lead)
> **Origin:** Owner Directive (`OWNER_ASKS.md`, 14 October 2026)
> **Target Brief:** Fold into **Sidecar Brief 28** (`28-lab-choreography-and-vista.md` Act IX Window Heal & Credits) and **Brief 29** (`29-audio-5bus-and-juice.md`)
> **Date:** 14 October 2026
> **Status:** **APPROVED FOR PRODUCTION.**

## 1. Research Grounding: Why Dry, Character-Driven Ending Songs Land So Well

We reviewed the design and reception of [Portal's "Still Alive"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Still_Alive) and composer [Jonathan Coulton's production notes](https://www.jonathancoulton.com/2007/10/15/portal-the-skinny/) to isolate why a sung epilogue from the player's lab mentor works so memorably:

1. **The Contrast Between Technical Jargon and Catchy Acoustic Warmth:** Pairing deadpan systems-engineering vocabulary (*four floats, twelve kilowatts, uncompiled dirt, recursive kernels*) with a breezy, melodic indie-folk/synth-pop arrangement turns the game's core rules into an earworm.
2. **Earned Affection Hidden Behind Dry Wit:** Dr. Gwen Haddy spent the campaign guiding the player through breakers, brownouts, and archive leaks with dry, clipped competence. Hearing her drop her guard just enough to sing a wry victory report over the Lab radio as the Earth window heals makes the player feel genuinely appreciated.
3. **The Arrangement Mirrors the Game's Core Mechanic:** Just as our world climbs from 1-bit wireframe/dither to full Suit-Cam PBR, the song's instrumentation **climbs the audio fidelity ladder** from a lone 1-bit square-wave beeper in Verse 1 to a full, warm stereo band by the final chorus.

## 2. Production Prompt for RUN.world / ElevenLabs Music Generator

> **Hard Rule:** Zero named songs, games, or artists appear in the generation prompt below.

- **Target Duration:** `130–145 seconds` (`~2:15`)
- **Style / Genre Prompt for ElevenLabs / RUN.world:**
  > `Dry, witty indie-electronic folk-pop ballad sung by a clear, articulate female alto voice with warm, deadpan British-transatlantic scientist delivery. Starts sparse and intimate with a retro 8-bit square-wave arpeggio and ticking studio relay click at 96 BPM in D Major. Gradually builds across verses: adding crisp fingerpicked acoustic guitar and 16-bit FM synth bass in the first chorus, then blooming into a lush, warm full-band arrangement with analog synth pads, melodic bass, brushed drums, and shimmering piano chords by the final chorus. Melodic, catchy, bittersweet, and triumphant.`

## 3. Stage-by-Stage Musical Arrangement Ladder

| Timestamp | Song Section | Fidelity Stage Mirror | Instrumentation & Mix Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`0:00 – 0:28`** | **Intro & Verse 1** | **Stage 0 (`Wireframe / 1-Bit`)** | 1-bit piezo square-wave melody + `50 Hz` Lab relay click; Haddy's voice starts with subtle radio band-pass (`320 Hz–3.4 kHz`). |
| **`0:28 – 0:58`** | **Verse 2 & Chorus 1** | **Stage 1–2 (`EGA / VGA`)** | Band-pass opens to full vocal clarity; 8-bit pulse counter-melody + fingerpicked acoustic guitar + 4-op FM bass enter. |
| **`0:58 – 1:35`** | **Verse 3 & Bridge** | **Stage 3–4 (`Gouraud / Hydro`)** | Brushed snare, warm electric bass, and Rhodes piano join; stereo width expands as the Lab Window Breach zips shut. |
| **`1:35 – 2:15`** | **Final Chorus & Outro** | **Stages 5–6 (`Full Biosphere`)** | Lush polyphonic synth strings + vocal harmonies + acoustic guitar strumming, ending on one quiet, nostalgic 1-bit beeper ping. |

## 4. Complete Original Lyrics: "Four Floats (Not Really Dirt)"

```text
[Intro: Sparse 8-bit square-wave arpeggio and rhythmic relay click]

[Verse 1: Intimate, deadpan female alto vocal, minimal backing]
You woke up on concrete with the breakers all tripped,
A sky full of static and the polygons stripped.
I told you "Don't touch that red button," and yet
You pulled every lever I had on the set.
We stepped through the doorway to wireframe stone,
Just lines in the dark and a drill of your own.

[Verse 2: Fingerpicked acoustic guitar and warm FM synth bass enter]
You fed fifty dirt to the teeth of the mill—
Though it's not really dirt, if we'reshooting for real.
You blew out the gate's little twelve-kilowatt line,
Then patched up the schema and said it was fine.
From one-bit to sixteen, the craters took shape,
Held together with cartridges, salvage, and tape.

[Chorus: Catchy, upbeat rhythm with brushed drums and bright synth chimes]
And it's four floats, baby, running in the dark:
Pixels for the colour and the vertices for spark,
Light to paint the morning on a freshly minted sea,
Compiling all the water where the craters used to be.
No, a simulation can't sustain a simulation long—
Unless an engineer steps in and proves the kernel wrong.

[Verse 3: Full warm band arrangement, melodic bass and piano]
We sealed up the rifts where the nineties leaked through,
Old sprites in the basin that charging at you.
Poor Vance left his notes on the rim of the ridge,
Trying to hot-patch the fault in the Bridge.
He thought we were finished; he didn't foresee
A stubborn technician with a Studio key.

[Bridge: Shimmering analog synth pads, slightly quieter and reflective]
Now look out the window—the column is gone,
The storm's clearing out and the grass is switched on.
Eleven new domes are all pinging the board,
And who's running the server where *our* world is stored?
Let's... not pull that thread while the coffee is hot.
I'm frankly amazed that we kept what we've got.

[Chorus: Full triumphant harmonic bloom, strings and chip counter-melody]
'Cause it's four floats, baby, running in the dark:
Pixels for the colour and the vertices for spark,
Light to paint the morning on a freshly minted sea,
Compiling all the water where the craters used to be.
No, a simulation can't sustain a simulation long—
Unless an engineer steps in and proves the kernel wrong.

[Outro: Warm acoustic chord fading back to a single 8-bit beeper note]
The Studio's open. The telemetry's green.
Best damned one-kilometre moon that I've seen.
 Don't touch the red button on your way out the door...
See you on the lattice, Sector Zero-Four.
```

# 26b — "Four Floats" v2: the rhythm rewrite the owner liked

> **Author:** Claude Opus, from Argo's plan 26 (his concept, story and images), after the owner's review of v1.
> **Date:** 14 October 2026
> **Status:** v2 is the ending and credits song (`apps/web/public/audio/music-ending.mp3`, from `zips/runworld/music/four-floats-v2.mp3`). The owner: "i like it, its a banger".

## Why v2
The owner on v1: "it feels like its missing a beat and 8bit background music and the words feel too accurate, the singer is having to force a rythm with words that dont fit that shape".

v2 keeps Argo's story and jokes, and changes three things:
- **A strict, singable meter:** verses alternate 5- and 7-syllable lines, with every stress on a beat; the bridge is even 6-syllable lines.
- **A repeating hook:** "Four floats in the dark".
- **The beat:** a drum machine from bar one, with 8-bit arpeggios and a pulse bass under the whole song. The arrangement still climbs the fidelity ladder.

**Still to do (the owner):** "it ends on the words sector 4 and just stops, i recomend popping in the courus with no vocals after that and loop it".

## Production prompt (RUN.world, ElevenLabs music, 150 s, 563 credits)
```text
Catchy, upbeat chiptune synth-pop at 120 BPM in D major. A steady four-on-the-floor drum machine beat (punchy kick, crisp snare on 2 and 4) from the very first bar to the end. Bright 8-bit square-wave arpeggios and a bouncing pulse-wave bassline run under the whole song. Sung by a warm, dry, witty female alto with a deadpan, slightly sardonic delivery, short punchy phrases that land exactly on the beat, and a big, simple singalong chorus hook. The arrangement builds: the first verse is pure 8-bit chip with the drum machine; the second verse adds a fat 16-bit FM bass and soft synth pads; the final choruses add live drums, warm analog synths and stacked vocal harmonies, still over the 8-bit arpeggios. Ends on one single chiptune beep.

Lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Lights out, breakers down,
static where the sky should be.
Told you, "Don't pull that,"
you pulled it, naturally.

[Verse 2]
Wireframe moon, so cold,
just the lines and not the stone.
Then your mill came on
and the pixels came back home.

[Pre-Chorus]
One bit, sixteen, two-five-six,
turn it up, turn it up.

[Chorus]
Four floats in the dark,
pixels, vertices and light,
pour a little water
and the moon comes back tonight.
Four floats in the dark,
watch it render, line by line.
It's not really dirt,
but the world is looking fine.

[Verse 3]
Sprites from ninety-three
crawling out to say hello.
Seal them with the beam,
send the archive down below.

[Verse 4]
Vance went out alone,
lost his signal on the ridge.
You had me, and tape,
and a Studio, and the Bridge.

[Pre-Chorus]
One bit, sixteen, two-five-six,
turn it up, turn it up.

[Chorus]
Four floats in the dark,
pixels, vertices and light,
pour a little water
and the moon comes back tonight.
Four floats in the dark,
watch it render, line by line.
It's not really dirt,
but the world is looking fine.

[Bridge]
Look out the window now,
the tear is sewing shut,
the grass is switching on.
Don't ask who's running us.

[Final Chorus]
Four floats in the dark,
pixels, vertices and light,
pour a little water
and the moon comes back tonight.
Four floats in the dark,
watch it render, line by line.
It's not really dirt,
but the world is looking fine.

[Outro]
Don't touch the red one.
See you, Sector Four.
```
